dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL-style multi-program source file using BINARY-CHAR, LINE SEQUENTIAL, SHARING WITH ALL, and COPY with REPLACING; no IBM-specific extensions detected
evidence: end program asmzx / end program asmxbin etc.

purpose.domain_detail: Assembler/linker toolchain: a two-pass assembler that reads assembly source, resolves defines and symbols, encodes instructions to binary output
purpose.summary: This program (asmzx) is a COBOL-implemented assembler. It reads an assembly source file (program.asm), processes define and symbol directives, expands macros, parses instructions with up to three operands, and writes symbol/instruction records. Companion sub-programs (asmxbin, asmxopcd, asmxglen, asmxcasu, asmxexpn) handle binary encoding, opcode lookup, instruction length calculation, case conversion, and macro expansion respectively.

notable_features: Multiple nested programs in a single source file (END PROGRAM boundaries)
Indexed file I/O for symbol and define tables
SHARING WITH ALL on file open
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
Custom opcode encoding logic (binary bit manipulation)
verdict.notes: Source truncated at 16000 chars; the asmxcasu program body is cut off. Dialect is likely GnuCOBOL based on BINARY-CHAR and LINE SEQUENTIAL usage, but no compiler directive confirms this. The assembler appears to target a custom/toy ISA given the simple opcode modes (a-e) and nibble-based encoding.
